This page installs SCGSim 2.0.0 and the public component library used by the tutorials. Use a separate `uv` project for each study so its Python packages and lockfile stay together. Installing SCGSim does not install Palace or AEDT; set those up separately on the computer that runs the solver.

The PDK installs as `orpen-sc-pdk` and imports as `orpen_sc_pdk`. The tutorial environment below uses the SimplePad source. Circular Pad and flip-chip Xmon examples use separate environments and PDK sources.

::: {.callout-note title="Before you start"}
- Python 3.12 or 3.13.
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).
- For AEDT workflows: a Windows or Linux computer with AEDT 2024.2 and a licence.
:::

## Step 1: Create a study environment {#step-1-create-a-study-environment}

Create a project with Python 3.12. `uv` creates and manages its `.venv` and lockfile:

```bash
uv init --python 3.12 scgsim-study
cd scgsim-study
```

Python 3.13 is also supported. This example uses Python 3.12.

## Step 2: Install SCGSim and the tutorial PDK {#step-2-install-scgsim-and-the-tutorial-pdk}

Add the stable SCGSim source, the SimplePad PDK source, the extras used by the beginner tutorials and `ipykernel` to this project:

```bash
uv add 'scgsim[palace,aedt-epr,visualization] @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim.git@e66c5641404c0d0baed023a2cf2bc9e1e798b2e2' \
  'orpen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk.git@51985d9507025e8241205712e866c0b804de29b9' \
  ipykernel
```

`uv add` records these dependencies in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`. Run Python commands from this project with `uv run` so they use this environment.

| Extra | Use it to | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| *(none)* | Read returned results and show reports | NumPy, Plotly |
| `palace` | Prepare Palace runs | GDSFactory 9.x, GDS reader, Gmsh |
| `aedt` | Prepare HFSS, Q3D or Q2D runs | GDS reader, PyAEDT 1.3.0 |
| `aedt-epr` | Prepare HFSS runs with surface EPR from a component | `aedt` plus GDSFactory 9.x and KLayout 0.30.x |
| `visualization` | Render 3D previews of prepared geometry | Mesh reader, image tools, PyVista |

Combine extras with commas in the package requirement. Geometry previews need a working OpenGL or EGL context; see [Geometry preview](../geometry-preview.qmd) for headless options.

## Step 3: Check the installation {#step-3-check-the-installation}

Run this from the study project:

```bash
uv run python -c "from importlib.metadata import version; import orpen_sc_pdk; print(version('scgsim')); print(version('orpen-sc-pdk'))"
```

The command prints the installed SCGSim and PDK versions and confirms that the PDK import works. Record both versions with your study.

<a id="step-5-set-up-the-solver-host"></a>

## Step 4: Set up the solver host {#step-4-set-up-the-solver-host}

You can prepare runs on one computer and run the solver on another. The solver host needs:

- **Palace:** a `palace` executable, or a wrapper script that starts it with MPI. If your cluster uses environment modules, note the `module load` command; you pass it to SCGSim when preparing a run. See the [Palace installation guide](https://awslabs.github.io/palace/stable/install/).
- **AEDT:** AEDT 2024.2, a licence, and PyAEDT 1.3.0 in the Python environment that runs the generated script. The script starts AEDT, saves the project and closes AEDT when it finishes.

Reading returned results needs only SCGSim; it does not need Palace or AEDT.

## Environments for other examples {#example-environments}

Create a separate `uv` project for each example below. Each project pins its own PDK source and adds the same stable SCGSim source with the extras that example needs. Keep these environments separate from the beginner tutorial project.

### Circular Pad {#env-circular-pad}

Used by the [Circular Pad LC study](palace-eigenmode.qmd#circular-pad-lc-study). Create a new environment for the Palace example:

```bash
uv init --python 3.12 circular-pad-study
cd circular-pad-study
uv add 'scgsim[palace,visualization] @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim.git@e66c5641404c0d0baed023a2cf2bc9e1e798b2e2' \
  'orpen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk.git@ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52' \
  ipykernel
```

### Flip-chip Xmon {#env-xmon}

Used by the [flip-chip Xmon example](../tutorial-xmon-input.qmd). This environment includes both Palace and AEDT EPR preparation:

```bash
uv init --python 3.12 xmon-study
cd xmon-study
uv add 'scgsim[palace,aedt-epr,visualization] @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim.git@e66c5641404c0d0baed023a2cf2bc9e1e798b2e2' \
  'orpen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk.git@35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9' \
  ipykernel
```
